svg.aria-label: A hedged Payer. A Payer deposits 1,000 and Receivers 2,000, so R over P is 2. The Collateral Vault pays 5 percent, so the Payer earns 50 a year on its own deposit and 100 a year of funding from the Receivers. The Payer is short 2,000 of the price, 1,000 times R over P, and hedges with a long 2,000 position on another venue, so price risk cancels. If the hedge costs 3 percent a year on 2,000, that is 60, and the Payer keeps about 90 a year, or 9 percent. If Receivers grow to 4,000, funding doubles, but so does the short and the hedge needed.
svg.title: A hedged Payer
